The earlier Brevig--Ortega-Cerdà--Seip paper establishes the related Riesz-projection exponent-4 threshold but does not state the finite-radius Poisson deficit. Direct statement-level comparisons and literature searches found no broader result implying this exact all-radius family formula.
residual_risks: An equivalent finite-radius identity could exist under substantially different notation in literature not surfaced by the searches.
The result does not address perturbations of the obstruction family, so it supplies evidence about one sharpness mechanism rather than a structural proof of the full endpoint conjecture.

value.rationale: The source identifies \(p=4\) as the unresolved endpoint and the treated family as the mechanism proving every \(p>4\) fails. An exact all-radius endpoint deficit for that canonical family is therefore a motivated boundary result: it rules out the immediate supercritical witness as an endpoint counterexample and provides a closed-form positive certificate useful for testing prospective endpoint arguments. The claim is narrow but mathematically natural and not an arbitrary parameter slice.
